movement_source: row 'Net interest margin (%)', column 30 Jun 25 -> column 30 Jun 26
headline: CBA's Group net interest margin (cash basis) decreased 3 basis points year-on-year, from 2.08% in FY25 to 2.05% in FY26. The decline was driven by 5 bps of headwind from asset pricing (home and business/institutional lending competition), partially offset by 5 bps tailwind from capital and replicating portfolio earnings, 2 bps from favourable portfolio mix (business lending and deposit growth), and 3 bps drag from growth in liquid assets. Funding costs and basis risk were flat. Excluding liquid assets, underlying margin was stable.

drivers.narrative: Growth in liquid assets averaged $187 billion, up $15 billion or 9% on the prior year. The bank states that liquid assets 'have broadly neutral impacts on net interest income' yet the walk attributes a -3 bps margin drag to this line.
Home lending pricing contributed -4 bps and business/institutional lending pricing contributed -1 bps, primarily reflecting the impact of competition in the mortgage market.
The bank states funding costs were flat year-on-year, with competitive deposit pricing largely offsetting the benefit of falling cash rates.
Favourable asset mix from strong growth in business lending ($27 billion or 10% increase to $299 billion average) and favourable funding mix from strong growth in deposits contributed +2 bps.
The bank states basis risk was flat year-on-year.
Higher earnings on the replicating portfolio due to changes in portfolio rate and volume (+4 bps) and higher earnings on capital hedges (+1 bps) drove a +5 bps contribution.
Lower risk management income in Treasury and growth in reverse sale and repurchase agreement balances drove a -2 bps contribution.

limitations: The results presentation slide (p60) presents a slightly different bar decomposition: Liquids & repos at -4 bps (vs -3 bps for Liquids alone in the results book), and combines Interest rate risk hedging at +5 bps without a separate Treasury & Markets bar (-1 vs -2). Both walks sum to -3 bps. The results book framing is used as primary per source hierarchy.
No statutory NIM figure is separately disclosed; the KPI table footnote states 'Presented on a cash basis unless stated otherwise', so the unlabelled NIM row takes the cash basis.

The Bank's net interest margin decreased by 3 basis points on the prior year to 2.05%. Excluding growth in liquid assets, which have broadly neutral impacts on net interest income, net interest margin was stable.

Asset pricing: Decreased margin by 5 basis points driven by home lending pricing (down 4 basis points) and business and institutional lending pricing (down 1 basis point), primarily reflecting the impact of competition.
Portfolio mix: Increased margin by 2 basis points driven by favourable asset mix from strong growth in business lending and favourable funding mix from strong growth in deposits.

Capital, Replicating and Other: Increased margin by 5 basis points driven by higher earnings on the replicating portfolio due to changes in portfolio rate and volume (up 4 basis points) and higher earnings on capital hedges (up 1 basis point).
Treasury and Markets: Decreased margin by 2 basis points due to lower risk management income in Treasury and growth in reverse sale and repurchase agreement balances.
